results.title: r/PHP on Reddit: What is the perfect email regex to use?
results.snippet: There is a "perfect" email regex but it is massively long. I think it's either in one of my Perl books or in Mastering Regular Expressions. However, the best idea is not to bother ... have some basic validation (matches .+@.+) and then send them an email they have to click on to confirm.

results.snippet: You'll find that the MailAddress class in .NET 4.0 is far better at validating email addresses than in previous versions. However, something like "I am me"@[10.10.10.10] does work! :) 2009-12-15T11:24:29.87Z+00:00 ...
